KIN 110.title: Human Anatomy
KIN 110.description: The basic structure and function of human anatomy. Emphasis is on the neural, muscular, and skeletal systems. Please consult the School of Kinesiology Credit Exclusion Lists:

KIN 120.title: Health and Exercise Management
KIN 120.description: Role of physical activity in the maintenance of a healthy life. Application of basic physical fitness and exercise methods, exercise techniques and fitness appraisal.

KIN 131.title: Neural and Musculoskeletal Physiology
KIN 131.description: Structure and function of the skeletal system, muscular system, integumentary system, neuro-hormonal control, and endocrinology. Emphasis will be to develop an understanding of the integrative nature of the systems discussed. Please consult the School of Kinesiology Credit Exclusion Lists:

KIN 132.title: Visceral Anatomy and Physiology
KIN 132.description: Structure and function of the cardiovascular system, respiratory system, urinary system, digestive system, and immune system. Emphasis will be to develop an understanding of the integrative nature of the systems discussed. Please consult the School of Kinesiology Credit Exclusion Lists:

KIN 140.title: Lifespan Motor Development
KIN 140.description: A lifespan approach to motor development that examines underlying factors affecting physical growth, physical activity behaviour, and human motor performance, while highlighting contemporary issues and trends in society. .

KIN 150.title: Sport and Exercise Psychology
KIN 150.description: Psychological theories and research related to sport and exercise behaviour. Please consult the School of Kinesiology Credit Exclusion Lists: .

KIN 160.title: Leisure and Sport in Society
KIN 160.description: Introduction to the political, economic and social basis of leisure and sport; concepts, theories and problems. .

KIN 205.title: Research Methods in Kinesiology
KIN 205.description: Critical evaluation of research studies and methods with emphasis on the physical activity context. Please consult the School of Kinesiology Credit Exclusion Lists:

KIN 206.title: Introduction to Statistics in Kinesiology
KIN 206.description: Basic concepts and principles of descriptive and inferential statistics, and distribution-free statistical techniques. Please consult the School of Kinesiology Credit Exclusion Lists:

KIN 211.title: Human Motor Behaviour I
KIN 211.description: Processes underlying human movement and learning motor skills and factors influencing acquisition, performance, and movement control. .
KIN 211.prerequisiteText: All of (a) KIN_V 110 or HES_O 120 and (b) KIN_V 131 or HES_O 101 or BIOL_O 131

KIN 216.title: Biomechanics I
KIN 216.description: Application of elementary principles of physics and math to a quantitative analysis of movement. Analysis will also focus on the development of forces within muscles and their effect on initiating and controlling human movement. .

KIN 220.title: Exercise Testing and Prescription for Healthy Individuals with Special Considerations
KIN 220.description: Pre-exercise screening, exercise testing, and exercise prescription for improving health and performance for the general population and low-risk populations with special considerations.
KIN 220.prerequisiteText: All of (a) KIN_V 110 or HES_O 120 and (b) KIN_V 120 and (c) KIN_V 131 or BIOL_O 131 or HES_O 101 and (d) KIN_V 132 or BIOL_O 133 or HES_O 111

KIN 232.title: Nutrition, Physical Activity, and Health
KIN 232.description: Study of nutrition and its application to physical activity and health. Macro- and micronutrient classification and recommended daily intakes, their digestion, functions in the body and their role in supporting physical activity and health will be discussed. .
KIN 232.prerequisiteText: All of (a) KIN_V 131 or BIOL_O 131 or HES_O 101 and (b) KIN_V 132 or BIOL_O 133 or HES_O 111

KIN 235.title: Exercise Physiology I
KIN 235.description: Acute and chronic effects of exercise on body systems; basic concepts of cardiovascular, respiratory and muscular responses to physical activity. .
KIN 235.prerequisiteText: All of KIN_V 110, KIN_V 120, KIN_V 131, KIN_V 132

KIN 262.title: Health Policy and Society
KIN 262.description: Health policy and the social context in relation to active health. .

KIN 272.title: Field Work in Exercise Training for Healthy Aging
KIN 272.description: Opportunity to gain hands-on experience working with qualified exercise professionals to improve cardiovascular and musculoskeletal fitness in healthy middle aged and older adults using evidence-based group exercise programming. Restricted to students in the B.Kin. program with second-year standing or above. Pass/Fail.

KIN 300.title: Human Athletic Performance
KIN 300.description: An exploration of human movement and related issues pertaining to sports and athletic performance. Restricted to non-B.Kin. students only. Not for credit in the B.Kin. Program.

KIN 310.title: Human Functional Musculoskeletal Anatomy
KIN 310.description: The musculoskeletal structures and neural innervations involved in the control of human movement. Attention will be given to surface anatomy and to the practical application of human anatomy as it pertains to clinical, athletic, or everyday situations.

KIN 311.title: Sensorimotor Control of Human Movement
KIN 311.description: Processes and mechanisms involved in the sensory, perceptual, and cognitive contributions to human movements.
KIN 311.prerequisiteText: All of (a) KIN_V 110 or HES_O 120 and (b) KIN_V 131 or BIOL_O 131 or HES_O 101 and (c) KIN_V 211 and (d) KIN_V 216 or HES_O 102

KIN 313.title: Neuromuscular Integration of Human Movement
KIN 313.description: The neurophysiological and functional neuroanatomical processes involved in the sensory and motor control of movement, posture and balance in the human. Peripheral and central sensorimotor structures, and neurological diseases that affect human movement and balance control will be discussed.
KIN 313.prerequisiteText: All of (a) KIN_V 110 or HES_O 120 and (b) KIN_V 131 or BIOL_O 131 or HES_O 101

KIN 316.title: Biomechanical Properties of Tissues
KIN 316.description: Mechanics of muscular contraction and how the mechanical properties of the muscle, ligaments, tendons, and bone work synergistically.
KIN 316.prerequisiteText: All of (a) KIN_V 110 or HES_O 120 and (b) KIN_V 131 or BIOL_O 131 or HES_O 101 and (c) KIN_V 211 and (d) KIN_V 216 or HES_O 102

KIN 318.title: Programming and Data Science for Kinesiology
KIN 318.description: Think algorithmically to process, visualize, and analyze data related to various research questions. Through a combination of readings, lectures, tutorials, and problem sets, students will learn some of the most important tools and techniques in the Python data science ecosystem. Please consult the School of Kinesiology Credit Exclusion Lists: Restricted to students with third-year standing.
KIN 318.prerequisiteText: All of (a) KIN_V 110 or HES_O 120 and (b) KIN_V 131 or BIOL_O 131 or HES_O 101 and (c) KIN_V 211 and (d) KIN_V 216 or HES_O 102

KIN 320.title: Exercise Prescription and Behaviour Change for Individuals with Chronic Disease and Disability
KIN 320.description: Exercise prescription and behavioural support strategies for promoting health-enhancing levels of fitness for populations with chronic disease and disability.
KIN 320.prerequisiteText: All of (a) KIN_V 110 or HES_O 120 and (b) KIN_V 120 and (c) KIN_V 205 or HES_O 240 and (d) KIN_V 206 or HES_O 340

KIN 324.title: Prevention of Athletic Injuries
KIN 324.description: Training and safety strategies for the prevention of injuries to the musculoskeletal system and sense organs.

KIN 330.title: Clinical Exercise Physiology
KIN 330.description: Explore the physiological, pathological, and pharmacological factors influencing exercise responses and prescription in clinical populations. Emphasis is on cardiovascular, pulmonary, metabolic, renal, cancer-related, and autoimmune conditions, integrating diagnostic assessment, exercise testing, and safety considerations.
KIN 330.prerequisiteText: All of KIN_V 110, KIN_V 120, KIN_V 131, KIN_V 132, KIN_V 235

KIN 335.title: Advanced Applications of Exercise Physiology
KIN 335.description: Explore how the cardiovascular and respiratory systems are regulated and integrated during exercise.
KIN 335.prerequisiteText: All of KIN 110, KIN 120, KIN 131, KIN 132, KIN 235

KIN 342.title: Creating Effective, Developmentally Appropriate, Physical Activity Learning Environments
KIN 342.description: The pedagogical skills and knowledge required to design, and implement, developmentally appropriate physical activities learning environments in a variety of settings.

KIN 344.title: Leisure Services for Persons with a Disability
KIN 344.description: Policy issues relating to leisure opportunities for persons with disabilities.

KIN 345.title: Foundations of Coaching
KIN 345.description: Methods of athletic conditioning, planning the program, psychology of training and coaching, athletic evaluation.

KIN 351.title: Physical Activity and Disability
KIN 351.description: Physical activity counselling, education programming principles, exercise considerations, and strategies for promoting inclusive physical activity for people with disabilities.

KIN 353.title: Current Topics in Exercise and Health Psychology
KIN 353.description: Exploring concepts, principles, and theories as they relate to the practice of promoting and supporting recommended physical activity for individuals and population groups. Particular attention will be directed at contemporary issues, controversies, evidence informed initiatives, and innovative new approaches.
KIN 353.prerequisiteText: KIN_V 150 or HES_O 131 and third-year standing

KIN 355.title: Applied Approaches to Childhood Movement
KIN 355.description: An exploration of current and emerging trends, challenges, and opportunities for supporting movement experiences throughout the childhood years. .

KIN 360.title: Sport, Peace, and Conflict
KIN 360.description: Relationships that sport and leisure have with peace, conflict, and social inequality in Canada and internationally.

KIN 363.title: Leisure, Sport and Popular Culture
KIN 363.description: Selected aspects of leisure and sport examined in relation to modern social structures and cultures.

KIN 364.title: The Modern Olympics: Power, Politics, and Performance
KIN 364.description: Examination of the Modern Olympic Games as an event with important political, economic, environmental, and cultural ramifications.

KIN 368.title: Indigenous Sport and Physical Culture in Settler Canada
KIN 368.description: Historical and contemporary issues in Canada that shape Indigenous sport and physical activity, health programs, and policies.

KIN 411.title: Neuroanatomy of Human Movement
KIN 411.description: Neuroanatomy of human motion in healthy and clinical populations.
KIN 411.prerequisiteText: All of (a) KIN_V 110 or HES_O 120 and (b) KIN_V 131 or BIOL_O 131 or HES_O 101 and (c) KIN_V 211 and (d) KIN_V 216 or HES_O 102

KIN 413.title: Sensori-Motor Control of Human Balance
KIN 413.description: Examining the sensory, motor, and biomechanical factors that contribute to human balance control during quiet standing and postural reactions to internal and external perturbations. Emphasis on understanding the characteristics of healthy balance control and changes associated with age and disease.
KIN 413.prerequisiteText: All of KIN 110, KIN 131, KIN 211, KIN 216, and third-year standing

KIN 415.title: Sensori-motor Neuroplasticity in Movement and Exercise
KIN 415.description: Concepts in neuroplasticity related to sensori-motor control of movement and exercise. The focus will be on plasticity (both adaptive and maladaptive) that arises because of either training or injury/non-use as it relates to movement control and exercise.
KIN 415.prerequisiteText: All of (a) KIN_V 110 or HES_O 120 and (b) KIN_V 131 or BIOL_O 131 or HES_O 101 and (c) third-year standing

KIN 418.title: Computational Modelling of Human Sensori-Motor Control and Learning
KIN 418.description: Learn the fundamentals of modeling human behavior, including Bayesian probability theory, learning algorithms, and simulation. Gain proficiency with simulating Bayesian and non-Bayesian models with Python code to use these approaches to address novel research questions.

children.raw: or another introductory Python programming course

KIN 418.prerequisiteText: KIN_V 206 or HES_O 340 and KIN_V 318, or another introductory Python programming course (e.g., CPSC_V 110, Python version of DSCI_V 100)

KIN 419.title: Laboratory Investigations in Neuromechanical Kinesiology
KIN 419.description: Integration and application of laboratory principles and techniques for experimental investigations of topics in neuromechanical kinesiology, including biomechanics, motor behaviour, and neurophysiology.
KIN 419.prerequisiteText: All of KIN_V 110, KIN_V 131, KIN_V 211, KIN_V 216

KIN 421.title: Advanced Exercise Prescription in Chronic Conditions: Evidence-Informed Practice
KIN 421.description: Chronic conditions and their presentation, comorbidities, medications, pathophysiological basis, and their effects on exercise response and capacity will be discussed. The aim is to build competence in evidence-informed decision-making when assessing and prescribing exercise for clients with complex chronic conditions.

KIN 422.title: Professional Practice in Kinesiology
KIN 422.description: Exploration of professional practice in Kinesiology, encompassing key concepts such as scope of practice, clinical communication skills, professional ethics, shared decision-making, team-based care, entrepreneurship, and evidence-informed practice. Interprofessional collaborative approach to client care, fostering skills crucial for effective on-the-job decision-making.
KIN 422.prerequisiteText: All of (a) KIN_V 120 and (b) KIN_V 205 or HES_O 240 and (c) KIN_V 206 or HES_O 340

KIN 423.title: Clinical Exercise Assessment
KIN 423.description: Conduct cardiovascular fitness, musculoskeletal, functional, and risk stratification testing, with specific consideration for populations living with chronic disease and disability.

prerequisite.raw: Restricted to students in the B.Kin. program with fourth-year standing

KIN 423.prerequisiteText: Restricted to students in the B.Kin. program with fourth-year standing

KIN 424.title: Medical Aspects of Sport and Exercise
KIN 424.description: Training and safety strategies for the management and prevention of disorders of internal organs and central nervous system. Topics include environmental and nutritional factors in conditioning and pre-event preparation.
KIN 424.prerequisiteText: All of (a) KIN_V 110 or HES_O 120 and (b) KIN_V 131 or BIOL_O 131 or HES_O 101

KIN 428.title: Indigenous Health and Wellness
KIN 428.description: The complex social, cultural, historical, and economic factors that shape health and wellness within Indigenous communities will be explored through extensive blended learning and experiential learning opportunities.

KIN 432.title: Sport Nutrition
KIN 432.description: Sport nutrition guidelines, physiological mechanisms of fuel use in the body, nutritional strategies to support weight change, hydration, and ergogenic aids the needs of special athlete populations.
KIN 432.prerequisiteText: All of (a) KIN_V 131 or BIOL_O 131 or HES_O 101 and (b) KIN_V 132 or BIOL_O 133 or HES_O 111 and (c) KIN_V 232 or HES_O 200

KIN 434.title: Exercise, Nutrition, and Metabolism
KIN 434.description: Exploring the physiological and biochemical changes that occur in skeletal muscle, adipose tissue, and liver following exercise. Interactions between exercise, nutrition, and commonly prescribed medications used for the treatment of diabetes and cardiovascular disease will also be examined.
KIN 434.prerequisiteText: All of KIN_V 232, KIN_V 235, and third-year standing

KIN 435.title: Pulmonary Physiology of Exercise
KIN 435.description: Operation of the lungs, chest wall, and ventilatory control mechanisms during dynamic whole-body exercise.
KIN 435.prerequisiteText: All of KIN 110, KIN 120, KIN 131, KIN 132, KIN 235, KIN 335

KIN 438.title: Skeletal Muscle Physiology: Molecular Adaptions to Training, Disuse and Aging
KIN 438.description: Cellular and molecular mechanisms of muscle adaptability to aerobic and resistance training, inactive and aging: signaling cascades controlling hypertrophy and atrophy, satellite cell contribution to muscle repair, and mitochondrial/ribosomal biogenesis. BIOL 112 or similar recommended.
KIN 438.prerequisiteText: All of KIN 110, KIN 120, KIN 131, KIN 132, KIN 235, KIN 335

KIN 442.title: Planning Physical Education, Sport and Exercise Programs
KIN 442.description: Processes, techniques and considerations in the planning, implementation and evaluation of physical education, sport and exercise programs in both public and private agencies.
KIN 442.prerequisiteText: All of KIN 140, KIN 262 and Third-year standing

KIN 444.title: Exploring Alternative Methods for Teaching Games and Sports
KIN 444.description: Examination of innovative, developmentally appropriate, conceptual and tactical approaches to team game instruction.

KIN 450.title: Inclusive Approaches to Sport Psychology
KIN 450.description: Examination of the psychological and behavioural processes of athletes from a social justice perspective. The focus will be on the role of social structures, sociocultural norms, power relations, and social identities in shaping athletes' perceptions and lived experiences in sport.
KIN 450.prerequisiteText: All of KIN_V 150, KINIV 160, and third-year standing

KIN 453.title: Understanding and Changing Physical Activity Behaviour
KIN 453.description: Examining the influence of psychological factors across different settings and populations, with a particular focus on interventions aimed at enhancing mental health. Understanding psychology can be used to design effective interventions at the individual and community level.

KIN 457.title: The Psychology of Team Effectiveness
KIN 457.description: Within sport and other contexts that demand high performance, humans often work together as part of teams. Discover what makes those teams effective, why some teams flourish and others flounder, and how we might develop better teams.

KIN 459.title: Psychobiology of Physical Activity
KIN 459.description: Exploration of the role of physical activity and exercise on brain health, mental health, and underpinning psychological and biological mechanisms. This course deepens students' capacity to read and interpret scientific evidence.

KIN 460.title: Aging, Health, and Society
KIN 460.description: Examination of current issues in the sociology of aging and health.

KIN 463.title: Hockey in Canadian Society
KIN 463.description: Examines Canadian society through the lens of hockey. Explores the deep and symbiotic relationship between the nation and the game and the implications this relationship has for social, political, and cultural life in Canada.

KIN 464.title: Health Promotion and Physical Activity
KIN 464.description: Current perspectives on health promotion and health education; design and implementation of health promotion strategies in a variety of arenas, particularly health promotion/education strategies aimed at encouraging physical activity.
KIN 464.prerequisiteText: All of KIN 150, KIN 160, KIN 205, KIN 262

KIN 465.title: Interculturalism, Health and Physical Activity
KIN 465.description: Examination of multiculturalism and interculturalism in the delivery of community-based physical activities for diverse populations; connections between physical activity and health in different cultural contexts. Community service learning and participation in culturally unfamiliar physical activities are core elements.

KIN 469.title: Restoring Wellness Through Indigenous Land-Based Practices
KIN 469.description: Examining how colonialism and settler colonialism altered Indigenous physical practices and concepts of wellness and consider how Indigenous peoples and their communities are reclaiming and reengaging with physical culture and land-based practices to restore and maintain their sense of well-being.
KIN 469.prerequisiteText: All of KIN_V 160, KIN_V 262, and third-year standing

KIN 471.title: Exercise Management of Chronic Neurological Balance and Mobility Conditions
KIN 471.description: Work with an inter-professional health team to assess and rehabilitate neurological balance and mobility deficits. Students will assist in the delivery of exercise-based rehabilitation at the Physical Therapy Rehabilitation Clinic and the BC Brain Well Program. Restricted to students in the BKIN program with third- or fourth-year standing. Pass/Fail.

KIN 473.title: Kinesiology Field Work in Primary Care Medicine
KIN 473.description: Work in a team-based primary care setting with patients focusing on exercise prescription and program delivery under the clinical care of family physicians, dietician, practice support coaches and kinesiologists. Restricted to students in the BKIN program with fourth-year standing. Pass/Fail.

KIN 475.title: Physical Activity Counselling and Prescription for People with Spinal Cord Injury
KIN 475.description: Gain hands-on experience working with members of the Physical Activity Research Centre at the Blusson Spinal Cord Centre. Apply skills in exercise testing, prescription, and physical activity counselling. Restricted to students in the BKIN program with third- or fourth-year standing. Pass/Fail.

KIN 479.title: Scientific Communication and Research Skills in Neuromechanical Kinesiology
KIN 479.description: Training in research methods, computational skills, and scientific dissemination related to neuromechanics research in Kinesiology. Students will learn the principles underlying scientific communication and apply these principles in the form of an oral dissemination of scientific results. Restricted to students in the BKIN program with third- or fourth-year standing. Pass/Fail.
KIN 479.prerequisiteText: Two of KIN_V 310, KIN_V 311, KIN_V 313, KIN_V 316, KIN_V 411, KIN_V 413, KIN_V 415, KIN_V 419

KIN 482.title: Advanced Seminar in Neuromechanics
KIN 482.description: Topics consider how neurological, cognitive, sensory, mechanical and muscular systems interact to control human motion and its response to the physical environment.

children.raw: Restricted to students in the BKIN program with fourth-year standing

KIN 482.prerequisiteText: Two of KIN_V 311, KIN_V 313, KIN_V 316, KIN_V 411, 413, 415, KIN_V 419. Restricted to students in the BKIN program with fourth-year standing

KIN 483.title: Advanced Seminar in Systems Biology, Exercise and Health
KIN 483.description: Topics examine the roles of physical activity and fitness on physiological systems and underlying cellular and metabolic mechanisms.

children.raw: Restricted to students in the BKIN program with fourth-year standing

KIN 483.prerequisiteText: Two of KIN_V 320, KIN_V 335, KIN_V 420, KIN_V 424, KIN_V 432, KIN_V 434, KIN_V 435, KIN_V 438. Restricted to students in the BKIN program with fourth-year standing

KIN 484.title: Advanced Seminar in Indigenous Sport, Physical Activity and Health
KIN 484.description: Topics explore the relationship between Indigenous physical cultures, physical activity, health and wellbeing.

prerequisite.raw: Restricted to students in the BKIN program with third- or fourth-year standing

KIN 484.prerequisiteText: Restricted to students in the BKIN program with third- or fourth-year standing

KIN 485.title: Advanced Seminar in Leadership Education for Physical Activity
KIN 485.description: Topics consider health-related fitness, physical competence, cognitive understanding, and positive attitudes about physical activity.

prerequisite.raw: Restricted to students in the BKIN program with third- or fourth-year standing

KIN 485.prerequisiteText: Restricted to students in the BKIN program with third- or fourth-year standing

KIN 486.title: Advanced Seminar in Psychology of Movement
KIN 486.description: Topics examines the application of psychology to understanding and supporting healthy sport, physical activity, and health behaviors.

prerequisite.raw: Restricted to students in the BKIN program with third- or fourth-year standing

KIN 486.prerequisiteText: Restricted to students in the BKIN program with third- or fourth-year standing

KIN 487.title: Advanced Seminar in Sociocultural Studies
KIN 487.description: Topics explore the social, cultural and global context of sport, exercise, physical activity, health, and the body.

children.raw: Restricted to students in the BKIN program with fourth-year standing

KIN 487.prerequisiteText: Two of KIN_V 360, KIN_V 363, KIN_V 368, KIN_V 460, KIN_V 464, KIN_V 465, KIN_V 468. Restricted to students in the BKIN program with fourth-year standing

KIN 488.title: Advanced Seminar in Interdisciplinary Research in Kinesiology
KIN 488.description: Topics will be approached from multiple perspectives in a course designed to explore the interdisciplinarity of the field of kinesiology.

prerequisite.raw: Restricted to students in the BKIN program with fourth-year standing

KIN 488.prerequisiteText: Restricted to students in the BKIN program with fourth-year standing

KIN 490.title: Directed Studies in Kinesiology
KIN 490.description: Opportunity for students to conduct an independent study in a subject area of interest to them, under the direction of a KIN faculty member.

prerequisite.raw: Third-year standing and permission of the Associate Director, Undergraduate Program

KIN 490.prerequisiteText: Third-year standing and permission of the Associate Director, Undergraduate Program

KIN 492.title: Undergraduate Research Experience in Kinesiology
KIN 492.description: Opportunity for independent study that includes original data collection, under the direction of a KIN faculty member.

prerequisite.raw: Third-year standing and permission of the Associate Director, Undergraduate Program

KIN 492.prerequisiteText: Third-year standing and permission of the Associate Director, Undergraduate Program

KIN 501.title: Computational Methods for Data Acquisition and Signal Processing in Kinesiology
KIN 501.description: Hands-on laboratory course with an emphasis on developing critical computational research skills for the acquisition, processing and presentation of data related to human movements. Recommended prerequisite: Undergraduate degree in Kinesiology (or related field) including neuromechanical science courses.

KIN 515.title: Gap Analysis
KIN 515.description: Using analytics to obtain, describe, and visualize data to create a sport profile. Determine optimal programming decisions for coached athletes based on their performance pathway and gold medal profile. Apply research methods and principles of scientific inquiry, performance analysis, descriptive, prescriptive, and predictive analytics to improve athlete development and performance.

KIN 516.title: Psychology of Leadership and Group Processes
KIN 516.description: Contemporary theory, research and application with regard to leadership and group processes in the context of sport and exercise.

KIN 517.title: Business of High Performance Sport in Canada
KIN 517.description: Canada's sport system, its governance and stakeholders; financial management for high performance sport; communications, marketing, and sponsorship of high performance sport.

KIN 530.title: Directed Studies
KIN 530.description: Topics selected by the student, with the approval of the Graduate Advisor, can be studied under the supervision of a member of the faculty.

KIN 562.title: Bioenergetics of Physical Activity
KIN 562.description: Basic energy systems of the human body; primarily concentrating on the bioenergetics of the skeletal muscle cell, recovery from muscular work, substrate utilization, muscle fiber types, strength, endurance and the physiological assessment of maximal performance.

KIN 563.title: Measurement of Human Motion
KIN 563.description: A critical evaluation of research tools used to measure and assess human motor performance including electromyography, anthropometry, ergometers, indirect calorimetry, cinematography, and indirect dynamics.

KIN 564.title: Psycho-Social Aspects of Physical Activity
KIN 564.description: Selected psycho-social considerations in sport: initial and continuing involvement in the competitive sport environment.

KIN 565.title: Physiological Aspects of Physical Activity
KIN 565.description: Survey of research regarding the physiological aspects of activity; the effects of altitude and environmental temperature on man's performance in exercise and sports.

KIN 567.title: Skill Acquisition: Practice Design & Instruction
KIN 567.description: Research and theories on learning, maintaining, and excelling at movement skills, with a particular emphasis on sport. Effective practice conditions for learning and elite athletic performance.

KIN 568.title: Seminar in Human Sensorimotor Control
KIN 568.description: Reports and discussions of research literature concerning theories and findings in human sensorimotor control. Emphasis is given to understanding the basic mechanisms underlying sensorimotor control, utilizing frameworks drawn from motor behaviour, cognitive neuroscience, and neurophysiology.

KIN 570.title: Research Methods in Kinesiology
KIN 570.description: Research methods applied to the study of sport and physical activity, the nature of scientific inquiry, the design of experiments, the survey as a research medium, the historical and philosophical methods of inquiry, the writing of the research report.

KIN 571.title: Qualitative Methods in Sport, Leisure, and Health Studies
KIN 571.description: Theoretical, methodological, and ethical debates about and approaches to qualitative methods; issues in and approaches to qualitative inquiry. .

KIN 572.title: Research Methods for Sport & Health Sciences
KIN 572.description: Interpretation and evaluation of research methods and scientific findings related to coaching sciences and exercise and health-related professions.

KIN 573.title: Seminar in Mechanical Analysis of Human Movement
KIN 573.description: An investigation of human movement using cinematographical and other research methods. The case study approach will be used to examine kinesiological concepts and principles.

KIN 574.title: Seminar in Health Promotion Through Physical Activity
KIN 574.description: The relationship of new concepts in health to the promotion of health through physical activity; the application of research findings from a number of disciplines to the identification, selection, and targeting of health promotion/education strategies related to physical activity.

KIN 575.title: Principles of Applied Sports Analytics
KIN 575.description: Technical and applied knowledge in data science and analytics related to high performance sports.

KIN 580.title: Seminar in Body, Exercise, and Society
KIN 580.description: Personal, social, and cultural significance of the body in sport, exercise, and physical culture.

KIN 581.title: Sport, Leisure and Consumer Culture
KIN 581.description: Sport and leisure are viewed in the context of theoretical debates about mass society and consumer culture.

KIN 583.title: Physical Education, Sport and Exercise Programs
KIN 583.description: The development of curricula, implementation and evaluation techniques in physical education, sport and exercise programs; relationships of programs in schools, community centres and other institutions.

KIN 585.title: Performance Planning
KIN 585.description: Application of findings from sport profile and gap analysis to the planning and design of high performance training and coaching programs. Focuses on quadrennial, annual, meso and microcycle planning to integrate key factors that impact athlete performance and progression along the athlete development pathway.

KIN 586.title: Coaching Effectiveness
KIN 586.description: Analysis of athlete performance and appropriate design and application of coaching intervention and skill acquisition for athlete and coach development.

KIN 591.title: Seminar in the Organizational Analysis of Leisure
KIN 591.description: Selected topics in organizational theory as applied to the analysis of leisure and sport organizations.

KIN 596.title: High Performance Sport Inquiry
KIN 596.description: Blended learning approach in a problem-based setting. Students support their own research interests within the high performance sport arena.

KIN 597.title: Practical Applications in High Performance Sport
KIN 597.description: Apply and reflect on professional competency within existing coach or leader context in relevant High Performance sport environment.
